subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Desalination: Making Fresh Water from Salt
description: A short lesson to help you apply Desalination: Making Fresh Water from Salt.

hook.text: Oceans hold 97% of Earth's water — but you can't drink salt water.

buildup.text: Reverse osmosis pushes seawater through membranes that block salt.

discovery.text: High-pressure pumps force water through at 60+ bar. Energy is the big cost.

twist.text: Energy recovery devices reclaim pressure from the waste brine stream.

climax.text: Israel now gets over half its drinking water from desalination plants.

punchline.text: Push hard enough and the ocean gives up its fresh water.

quiz.question: What is the biggest cost in reverse osmosis desalination?
options: Replacing the membranes every few months
Energy to run the high-pressure pumps that force water through membranes
Disposing of the salt removed from the water
